summary: Gold, the metal: found in the earth, refined in the furnace, weighed out as wealth, tribute and spoil, and worked into the furnishings of the tabernacle and the temple and into idols. Because it is tried by fire and prized above all goods, it is the measure both of what Yahweh's words and wisdom surpass and of what cannot save in the day of his wrath; once (Zec 4:12) it is the golden oil the olive trees pour out. Scripture's Aramaic דְּהַב is the same word, the gold of Nebuchadnezzar's image and of the kingdom it stood for; Arabic ḏahab and Syriac dahbā show ḏ behind the ז.

words.summary: About 390 times, the commonest of scripture's words for gold (beside the rarer כֶּתֶם, פָּז and חָרוּץ, which are other roots). The brief's count includes the tokens of the names מֵי זָהָב (Gen 36:39; 1Ch 1:50) and דִּי זָהָב (Deu 1:1).

senses.definition: The precious metal, found in the ground, refined by fire, weighed out and worked: wealth, gift, tribute and spoil; the overlay and the vessels of the tabernacle and the temple; the material of idols.

evidence.note: The land of Havilah, “where there is gold”.
“And the gold of that land is good”: a thing found in a land, of better and worse quality.
“There is a mine for silver, and a place for gold which they refine (יָזֹקּוּ).”
“Its stones are the place of sapphire, and it has dust of gold.”
“The refining pot for silver and the furnace for gold, and Yahweh tests hearts.”
“Abram was very heavy in cattle, in silver and in gold”: gold as wealth.
The king “shall not greatly multiply silver and gold for himself”.
Pharaoh put “the chain of gold” on Joseph's neck.
Balaam: “If Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of Yahweh my God.”
Hezekiah's tribute: “three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold”.
David gave Ornan “shekels of gold by weight, six hundred”: gold weighed as payment.
The contribution for the sanctuary: “gold and silver and bronze”.
“You shall overlay it with pure gold (זָהָב טָהוֹר), inside and outside, and make a moulding of gold around it”: the ark.
“A lampstand of pure gold; of beaten work shall the lampstand be made.”
The inner room overlaid “with shut-up gold (זָהָב סָגוּר)”.
Two hundred shields of “beaten gold (זָהָב שָׁחוּט)”, six hundred of gold on each.
“And the gold was gold of Parvaim.”
“Gods of silver and gods of gold you shall not make for yourselves.”
“This people has sinned a great sin, and made themselves gods of gold.”
“I multiplied her silver, and gold, which they made for Baal.”
“Their silver and their gold they made into idols for themselves, that it may be cut off.”
“The smith overlays it with gold.”
“Behold, it is caught in gold and silver, and there is no breath at all within it.”
“Their idols are silver and gold, the work of man's hands.”
“We ought not to think that the Divine is like gold (χρυσῷ) or silver or stone, graven by art and man's device.”
From Sheba “they shall bring gold and frankincense, and proclaim the praises of Yahweh”.
The wise men offered the child “gold (χρυσὸν) and frankincense and myrrh”; the Peshitta's word is דַּהבָא.

senses.definition: Gold as what the furnace proves and purifies: the figure of Yahweh's testing of his people, by which the dross is taken away and what remains is true.

evidence.note: “I will refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested. He will call on my name, and I will answer him.”
“He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver; he will purify the sons of Levi and refine them as gold and as silver.”
“He knows the way that I take; when he has tested me, I shall come out as gold.”
“The refining pot for silver and the furnace for gold, and a man according to his praise.”
“The trial of your faith, much more precious than gold (χρυσίου) that perishes, though it is tried with fire.”
“Buy from me gold (χρυσίον) refined by fire, that you may be rich.”

senses.gloss: gold as the measure of worth
senses.definition: Gold as the highest earthly value, the measure that Yahweh's words, wisdom and a good name surpass, and that cannot deliver in the day of his wrath.

evidence.note: Yahweh's judgments are “more to be desired than gold, even much fine gold, and sweeter than honey”.
“The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver.”
“I love your commandments above gold, above fine gold.”
“A name is to be chosen rather than great riches, good favour rather than silver and gold.”
“There is gold and a multitude of rubies, but lips of knowledge are a precious vessel.”
“Apples of gold in settings of silver: a word spoken in its right time.”
Of wisdom: “gold and glass cannot equal it.”
“If I have made gold my hope, or said to fine gold, You are my confidence”: a sin Job denies.
“A ring of gold in a pig's snout: a beautiful woman without discretion.”
“Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of Yahweh.”
“They will cast their silver into the streets, and their gold will be an unclean thing.”
The Medes “who do not regard silver, and gold they do not delight in”.
“How the gold has grown dim, the good fine gold changed!”, of Zion's sons (4:2).
“The silver is mine and the gold is mine, says Yahweh of Armies.”

senses.definition: What has the colour of gold: the oil poured from the olive branches through golden pipes, and the golden splendour that comes from the north.

evidence.note: “The two olive branches which, through the two golden pipes, empty the gold (הַזָּהָב) out of themselves”: the oil that feeds the lampstand (4:2), called gold by its colour.
“Out of the north comes gold (זָהָב); with God is fearful majesty”: the brightness of the sky, or gold itself; the verse does not settle which.

evidence.locator: Exo.25.11; Exo.25.31; 1Ki.6.20; Job.28.1; Psa.19.11; Psa.119.72; Isa.60.6; Zec.13.9, זָהָב → χρυσίον; the commonest rendering, ×175

evidence.note: Faith tried by fire, more precious than χρυσίον: the testing of Zec 13:9.
“Redeemed not with corruptible things, silver or gold (χρυσίῳ).”
“Gold refined by fire.”
“The city was pure gold (χρυσίον καθαρόν)”: the זָהָב טָהוֹר of the sanctuary.
“Silver and gold I have none.”
“Your gold and silver is corroded”: the gold that cannot deliver (Zep 1:18).
Gold, silver, precious stones built on the foundation, and “the fire shall test each man's work”.
The golden altar of incense, the ark overlaid with gold, the golden pot of manna: the tabernacle's furnishings of Exo 25.
“Seven golden lampstands”, as the lampstand of Exo 25:31 and Zec 4:2.
“Idols of gold and silver and bronze and stone and wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk”, after Dan 5:23 and Psa 115:4.

parallels.note: Silver is named beside gold throughout: as wealth, as idols, as refined.
Fine gold, set beside זָהָב in parallel.
Another word for fine gold, in parallel.

words.summary: Twenty-three times in Daniel and Ezra: the Aramaic form of זָהָב, with ד for the older ḏ where Hebrew has ז.

senses.definition: Gold, the metal: the head of Nebuchadnezzar's dream image, the image he set up, the vessels of the house of God, the gods Belshazzar praised, the chain put on Daniel, and the gold sent with Ezra for the house of God.

evidence.note: “The head of this image was of good gold, its breast and arms of silver.”
“You are the head of gold”: Nebuchadnezzar's kingdom.
The stone cut without hands broke in pieces “the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold”.
“Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, its height sixty cubits.”
“We will not serve your gods, nor worship the image of gold which you have set up.”
“The vessels of gold and silver which Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem.”
“You praised the gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood and stone, which do not see or hear or know.”
“A chain of gold about his neck.”
“The vessels of the house of God, of gold and silver … shall be restored.”
“The silver and gold which the king and his counsellors have freely offered to the God of Israel.”

cognates.gloss: gold; (form IV and II) gild, overlay with gold
cognates.note: The same word as the Hebrew, with ḏ behind ז. Arabic also has a verb ḏahaba “go, go away” spelt with the same letters; nothing ties it to gold, and it is not counted as the Hebrew's sense. The gilding verb is made from the noun, as the Hebrew overlay is with צָפָה and the noun.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 983, art. ذهب, ذَهَبٌ (n14115)
evidence.note: “[Gold;] a certain thing well known … ذَهَبَةٌ is the n. un., signifying a piece of ذَهَب [or gold].”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 983, art. ذهب, أَذْهَبَ
evidence.note: “اذهبهُ … and ذهّبهُ … He gilded it; did it over with gold.”

cognates.note: The Peshitta's word for gold throughout the New Testament: the wise men's gold (Mat 2:11), the gold that perishes though tried by fire (1Pe 1:7), gold refined by fire (Rev 3:18); the participle מַדְהבָא “gilded” of the woman and the city (Rev 17:4; 18:16). Aramaic d shows the older ḏ, as Arabic.
Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud: the Targum renders the gold of Havilah (Gen 2:11) by it; in the Talmud “gold” in a note means a gold denar.

evidence.note: “gold. Targ. Gen. II, 11 … B. Bath. 166ᵃ ד׳ פריכא broken pieces of gold.”

doctrine.statement: Nebuchadnezzar saw an image whose head was of good gold, its breast and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze, its legs of iron and its feet part iron and part clay (Dan 2:31–33). Daniel told him, “You are the head of gold”, and after him would arise another kingdom inferior to his, a third of bronze and a fourth strong as iron (Dan 2:38–40). A stone cut out without hands struck the image on its feet, and the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were broken together and became like chaff that the wind carried away, “and the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled all the earth” (Dan 2:34–35). Daniel interpreted it: “In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed, and the kingdom shall not be left to another people; it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever” (Dan 2:44–45). From the verses: the gold, the most precious part of the image, is a kingdom of men, and it is broken with the rest; the kingdom that replaces them is God's, set up on the earth, filling the whole earth where the image stood.

Gold is tested and refined in the furnace (Pro 17:3; 27:21), and Yahweh uses the same figure of his dealings with his people: “I will bring the third part through the fire, and refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested; they will call on my name, and I will answer them; I will say, It is my people, and they will say, Yahweh is my God” (Zec 13:9). The messenger of the covenant “will purify the sons of Levi and refine them as gold and silver, that they may offer to Yahweh an offering in righteousness” (Mal 3:3). Job, not knowing why he suffered, said, “When he has tested me, I shall come out as gold” (Job 23:10). Peter applies it to believers in their trials: “the trial of your faith, much more precious than gold that perishes, though it is tested by fire, may be found to praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ” (1Pe 1:6–7); and Christ counsels the lukewarm to “buy from me gold refined by fire, that you may be rich” (Rev 3:18). From the verses: trial is the means by which God proves and purifies those he calls his own, and its outcome is shown at Christ's appearing.

Gold is what men trust and what they make gods of (Exo 32:31; Job 31:24; Psa 115:4), but the prophets say: “Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of Yahweh” (Zep 1:18; Ezk 7:19), and in that day men will throw their idols of gold to the moles and the bats (Isa 2:20). Yahweh says, “The silver is mine and the gold is mine” (Hag 2:8). Peter writes that believers were redeemed “not with corruptible things, silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot” (1Pe 1:18–19), and James warns the rich, “your gold and silver is corroded” (Jas 5:3). From the verses: gold belongs to God and perishes, so it can neither save from his judgment nor redeem; redemption is by the death of Christ.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key זהב (BDB g.al.aa root heading, g.al.ab the noun); Aramaic דְּהַב under its own root key דהב (xd.ac.ac). No verb of the root occurs in scripture; Arabic, Syriac and later Hebrew make one (gild) from the noun. Names: m.bt.ab מֵי זָהָב is names/mezahab (Gen 36:39; 1Ch 1:50). d.bg.ab דִּי זָהָב (Deu 1:1) is a place (TIPNR Dizahab@Deu.1.1), with no person to tag, and is left unassigned. Both name keys are counted by spelling on every unpointed זָהָב token (the brief marks them “also d.bg.ab, m.bt.ab”), so their counts are inflated. The sense “golden oil” rests on Zec 4:12 alone; Job 37:22 may be golden light or literal gold from the north, and is left as an example. Not consulted: Old and Imperial Aramaic (CAL); Payne Smith for ܕܗܒܐ beyond SEDRA; Sabaean ḏhb, which Wiktionary glosses “bronze” (SabaWeb, Biella not checked; if confirmed, a `possible` cognate with ḏ). Akkadian and Ugaritic use ḫurāṣu/ḫrṣ (the Hebrew חָרוּץ) for gold and show no ḏhb; the brief's Oracc matches on z-b (ezēbu “leave”, zâbu “melt”) share no sense and are not recorded. Klein compares צהב “gleam, be yellow” (Lev 13:30 צָהֹב): a lead only, not followed; the sounds (ṣ against ḏ) do not match. Open questions: (1) whether Zec 4:12's הַזָּהָב is the oil named by its colour or the gold of the lamp's fittings; (2) the doctrine statements are reasoned conclusions to review.
